issues.body:
## LAUNCH Release Preparation for v0.14.3

# Release Checklist Template

Use this checklist for every release to ensure nothing is forgotten.

## Pre-Release (Before Export)

- [ ] All target issues/features merged to main
- [ ] CHANGELOG.md updated with version and changes
- [ ] Version number updated in:
  - [ ] `godot/project.godot` (application/config/version)
  - [ ] All release scripts
- [ ] All tests passing (`pytest`)
- [ ] No GDScript warnings in Godot editor
- [ ] Game tested manually (smoke test)
- [ ] Git status clean (all changes committed)

## Export & Package

- [ ] Open Godot 4.5.1+
- [ ] Project  ->  Export  ->  Windows Desktop
- [ ] Export to: `builds/windows/vX.Y.Z/PDoom.exe`
- [ ] Verify both .exe and .pck files created
- [ ] Run `bash package_release.sh`
- [ ] Verify package created successfully

## Test Package

- [ ] Extract zip to clean directory
- [ ] Run PDoom.exe
- [ ] Test core gameplay:
  - [ ] Queue actions (AP tracking works)
  - [ ] Clear queue (C key works)
  - [ ] Remove individual items (✕ buttons work)
  - [ ] Commit turn (Space works)
  - [ ] Events display correctly
  - [ ] Save/load works
- [ ] Check for console errors

## GitHub Release

- [ ] Run `bash create_github_release.sh`
- [ ] Verify release created on GitHub
- [ ] Test download link works
- [ ] Release notes are correct

## Post-Release

- [ ] Update README.md with download link
- [ ] Close related issues with release note
- [ ] Commit post-release changes:
  ```bash
  git add README.md [other files]
  git commit -m "chore: Post-release updates for vX.Y.Z"
  git push origin main
  ```
- [ ] Update pdoom1.com website
- [ ] Announce on social media (if applicable)
- [ ] Create milestone for next version
- [ ] Move open issues to next milestone

## Rollback Plan (If Issues Found)

1. Delete GitHub release (DO NOT delete tag yet)
2. Fix issues locally
3. Re-export and re-package
4. Re-create GitHub release with same tag
5. Update download links if changed

## Version Number Guidelines

- **Patch (X.Y.Z)**: Bug fixes, minor tweaks
- **Minor (X.Y.0)**: New features, non-breaking changes
- **Major (X.0.0)**: Breaking changes, major overhauls

## Notes

- Keep this checklist updated as release process evolves
- Add platform-specific steps as Mac/Linux builds are added
- Consider automating more steps with GitHub Actions

issues.title: budget: his four answers applied, the assumption named, and the number they still do not license
issues.body:
Applies the money rulings from Monday **morning** (coordination `tools/atoms/memo_rulings_2026-08-24.jsonl`, atoms **M24-010 to M24-024**) and now Monday **afternoon** (`tools/atoms/memo_rulings_2026-08-24_afternoon.jsonl`, atoms **P24-020 to P24-025**) to `docs/copy/budget.json` and `tools/render_budget.py`. **Nothing published, nothing posted.** Pip publishes.

## `python tools/render_budget.py --check`

```
CHECK OK: 8 line items; min column $14,000, goal column $48,000; declared gap $500 reconciles.
Constraints carried (not machine-checkable, honour them):
  - NOBODY has been hired, commissioned, approached, quoted or engaged. Every figure is conditional. A single slip into past tense makes this a misrepresentation.
  - The game is free and source-available and stays that way. A pledge funds the work, not a licence, and not early access.
  - Never write the phrase 'open source'. The licence is an INTERIM source-available licence, all rights reserved; an open-source licence for the engine is only planned. The renderer greps the emitted page for it.
  - Do not type the raised total or days remaining. Link the page and let it resolve.
  - Do not identify the project's first backer, by name OR by description, until he has been asked.
  - p(Doom)1 is not finished. No copy may frame this as a launch, a 1.0, or a completed thing.
  - EVERY FIGURE ON THE PAGE IS US DOLLARS, and no second currency appears anywhere on it. Pip estimates in his own currency what he would pay people in Australia and converts it himself before it reaches this file; the conversion is his and is not shown. His words, 2026-08-24: 'just the US talking, consistent US figures, and just take my estimations what I am going to pay artists in Australia and convert it to US dollars -- it just adds math to people.' No dual-currency row, no parenthetical, no rate. The renderer greps the finished page for the other currency's marks.
```

Exit 0, and **no `NEEDS PIP` block follows it any more**. All three flags are cleared and none was added.

`--format html` builds: **30,188 bytes**, emitted-page guard passed. **Not published.** Per **P24-025** it is rendered where Pip can read it first:

```
D:\Local_Code\pdoom1-website\public\_review\funding-2026-08-24.html
```

`public/_review/` is gitignored in the website repository, so that is a local file and not a deployed page. Regenerate it with:

`python tools/render_budget.py --format html --out ../pdoom1-website/public/_review/funding-2026-08-24.html`

## Before / after

The "before" column is this PR's previous state, not `main`.

| line | min before | min after | goal before | goal after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hosting and infrastructure | $900 | $900 | $1,500 | $1,500 |
| Asset generation and tooling | $1,100 | $1,100 | $2,500 | $2,500 |
| Open dataset maintenance | $3,000 | $3,000 | $4,000 | $4,000 |
| Partial recovery of Pip's time | $5,000 | $5,000 | $12,000 | $12,000 |
| Minimum case: money moved off Pip's draw, not yet assigned | $4,000 | **line deleted** | — | — |
| Part-time gameplay developer | — | — | $17,000 | $17,000 |
| Directed art pass | — | — | $6,000 | $6,000 |
| Music: musicians, editor, mixer | — | **$2,400** | — | — |
| Community support | — | **$1,600** | $5,000 | $5,000 |
| **Total** | **$14,000** | **$14,000** | **$48,000** | **$48,000** |

Both column totals are unchanged, the $500 gap is untouched, and the line count drops from nine to eight because the holding line is dissolved rather than zeroed.

## P24-020 — the music currency

**Ruled: take the money off another line, do not raise the published goal.**

The line the money came off is **Pip's own draw**, cut from $9,000 that morning. So the music line carries **$2,400 in the minimum column and a dash in the goal column**, and the published goal is exactly $48,000, unmoved.

**The currency needed no conversion rate.** His own sentence gives a US figure — *"four musos at one session each, that's $2400 US"* — and **P24-024** rules the budget to consistent US figures. Using a figure he stated in US dollars is not choosing a rate. **No exchange rate appears anywhere in this diff.**

The dash in the goal column would read as an omission, so the page says out loud why it is there, and the sentence is emitted from the data (`min_only`), so it disappears if the shape ever changes.

## P24-024 — currency presentation, which governs the whole page

*"Just the US talking, consistent US figures... it just adds math to people."*

- The verbatim `"that's $2400 US, also AU, don't just back convert that to Australia"` is **removed from `budget.json`**, so it can no longer reach any rendering.
- `published.currency: "USD"` added, and a seventh entry in `constraints`.
- The page states it twice in reader-facing prose.
- **The guard gains a pattern**: `AUD`, `AU$`, `A$<digit>`, `Australian dollars`. It reads the emitted bytes, so `<html lang="en-AU">` — a house rule of the site — does not trip it, because the guard strips tags before matching.
- **Proved rather than asserted.** I injected `Also AUD 1,234 for good measure.` into a line item's basis and re-rendered:

```
REFUSING to emit the page.
  emitted 'AUD' -- a second currency on a page ruled to be consistent US figures only. Pip converts his own estimates before they reach the data and the conversion is not shown; constraint 7
```

## P24-022 — his own draw: the division is reversed

*"Even if I pay myself like $150 or $200 for a day, that gets me fewer days in the year, which is fine. So maybe I work on it once a fortnight."*

`implied_day_rates()` is **deleted** and replaced by `own_draw_days()`. The old function divided the column by a fixed `focused_days_per_year: 52` and published whatever rate fell out, which is how **$96 a day** reached a draft. The new one takes the rate as the input:

- **$150–$200 a day** is now a data point in `rates`, alongside the commercial and junior bands.
- **$5,000 buys 25–33 days.** A fortnightly rhythm is 26, which sits inside that, and the page says the rhythm falls out of the figure rather than being a schedule anybody is promising.
- **$12,000 buys 60–80 days** on the same division.
- `focused_days_per_year` is **removed from the data**, so there is no fifty-two left to regenerate $96 from. `check()` now requires the rate band instead of the divisor.
- Floor, not round, in `own_draw_days()`: a part-day is not a day, and rounding up would promise a day the money does not buy.

## P24-021 — where the freed $4,000 goes, and the one assumption in this PR

**Ruled: community support, and small payments for artists for session work.** The holding line is dissolved into those two.

**THE SPLIT IS AN ASSUMPTION, NOT A RULING.** He named two destinations and no proportion. Applied: **$2,400 to the musicians, $1,600 to community support.**

**Why not 50/50:** it would contradict a figure he stated himself. Four musicians at one session each is $2,400, so a $2,000 music line would sit under its own only-priced component. The split point is therefore his own figure and community support takes the balance. **That is a defensible choice and not his decision.** If he wants it the other way round, one number in `budget.json` changes and everything re-renders.

**A second, smaller assumption, stated:** "small payments for artists for session work" is read as the **music** line rather than the art line. "Session work" is the music line's own words — *four musicians at one session each* — and the art line's session language is about hourly-versus-per-output, not about a payment. If he meant the art line instead, the money moves and the goal column is unaffected either way.

## What was NOT derived, and is flagged rather than filled in

- **The editor's and the mixer's sessions have no rate behind them.** M24-015 named *"four musicians at one session each, about $600 each; plus one editor and one mixer"*. Only the musicians' half has a figure, so the music line carries **$2,400 and not a cent more**, and its `settled_by` says exactly what would close it.
- **The *"at least $3,000 on artists"* floor from M24-015 is not met by $2,400 and is not on the page.** That floor was stated with no currency marker and no destination. Reconciling it needs either a conversion rate or a decision about which lines count as "artists" — he gave neither. **One resolved ambiguity does not license resolving the other, so it is reported, not closed.**

## P24-023 — the Windows item, which the correction was missing

The USD 415–460 figure is the whole pre-compliance basket, not the macOS fix. **Confirmed**, and he ruled the page must say the Windows item too.

- New `windows_signing` block: not code-signed, certificate **$215–$260/year**, three-step plan (individual validation, cloud signing rather than a physical token, budget it as recurring under the 459-day cap).
- New `pre_compliance_basket`: three rows, and **the total is summed by the renderer, never typed** — $215–260 + $99 + $100 = **$414–$459**.
- `check()` reconciles the rows against `macos_signing` and `windows_signing` and fails if they drift apart. A correction that can drift from the figures it corrects is worse than no correction.
- `_source_rounds_it` records that `docs/release/CODE_SIGNING.md` says *"about USD 415-460"* while its own rows sum to $414–459. **The page publishes the sum, not the rounding.**
- The page does **not** claim Windows is the worse defect, only the more expensive to fix: the macOS build has never been verified to run at all, which is worse and cheaper.

## Two sentences that the arithmetic falsified and nothing would have caught

Moving $4,000 into the minimum column made these false:

- *"Nobody else is paid"* / *"Nobody else is paid anything"* → **"No illustrator and no developer is paid at this tier."**
- *"At $14,500 nothing is commissioned"* → **"At $14,500 no illustrator is paid at all."**
- *"partial recovery of one focused day a week"* → the day count now comes from the rate.

**They are prose, not figures, so nothing recomputed them.** This is the failure mode `budget.json` exists to prevent, operating one level up: the data was right and the sentences around it were not. Worth a rule of its own — moving money between columns changes what the surrounding prose is allowed to claim.

## Noted while committing, not fixed here

The `commitment-calendar` pre-commit hook indexes `docs/rulings/RULINGS.md`, which `generate_rulings.py` rewrites. **The two generated indices do not converge in one pass.** Four alternating passes were needed here before both hooks went green and the outputs were byte-stable. Reporting rather than fixing: it is not this PR's subject.

## Companion

`PipFoweraker/coordination#116` carries the page copy, whose table is pasted from `--format table` here, and whose rung ladder is recomputed: $1,600 of community support now sits inside the minimum, so its rung is **$3,400 landing at $40,400**, and the final rung is **$7,600 net** rather than $6,000.

issues.title: Release ledger: a version was bumped and never tagged
issues.body:
A value of `version.txt` has no matching git tag and no
declaration in `docs/releases/UNTAGGED.md`.

This issue is opened by `.github/workflows/release-ledger.yml`,
which is the only release trigger in this repo that fires on the
BUMP rather than on the tag. Everything else in the release
family is downstream of tagging and cannot see this state.

```
[release_ledger] STALE: docs/releases/RELEASE_LEDGER.md does not match generated content. Run --write.
[release_ledger] FAIL: 0.14.3 bumped 2026-08-23 (dd3039fd) has NO TAG and no declaration
```

## The two exits, and there are only two

1. **Push the tag.** That arms `enhanced-release.yml`, which
   builds all three platforms and publishes the release with
   assets. It is outward-facing and hard to reverse.
2. **Declare it** in `docs/releases/UNTAGGED.md` with the reason
   it stays internal.

Leaving it undecided is the state this workflow exists to end.

issues.title: guards: thirteen that ran nowhere but pre-commit, and three that could only ever pass
issues.body:
Closes the first act of #1265 and part of the second. Follow-up: #1297.

> "a drill that has never been run is the same as a guard that has never failed"
> -- docs/rituals/gate_6_board_opens.md

## 1. The census

`.pre-commit-config.yaml` has 36 hooks. This is which of them CI can see. The exact
command that produces it, run against this branch:

```
python tools/check_guard_parity.py --markdown
```

It is a command and not a table in a doc because a hand-maintained map of which guard
runs where is exactly the artefact this repo keeps watching rot (see the stale
`docs/game-design/decisions/README.md`). Three things it gets right that
`grep -rn <tool> .github/workflows/` does not:

1. A blanket `pre-commit run --all-files` in a workflow covers every hook at once. There
   is none here -- `grep -rn "pre-commit" .github/workflows/` returns one comment line
   in `enhanced-release.yml` and nothing else -- but a per-tool grep would have been
   wrong if there were.
2. A workflow may invoke a tool by bare basename rather than repo path. Both are searched.
3. **A tool can run in CI in the wrong MODE.** `scripts/generate_release_metadata.py`
   appears in `enhanced-release.yml` -- as `--version`, which REGENERATES the feed. The
   pre-commit hook runs `--check`, which GATES it. Grepping the filename says "covered".
   The gate is not covered at all. Reported PARTIAL, not YES.

| hook id | tool invoked | gating flag | in CI? | which workflow |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `trailing-whitespace` | (no project script) | | - | |
| `end-of-file-fixer` | (no project script) | | - | |
| `check-yaml` | (no project script) | | - | |
| `check-json` | (no project script) | | - | |
| `check-added-large-files` | (no project script) | | - | |
| `check-case-conflict` | (no project script) | | - | |
| `check-merge-conflict` | (no project script) | | - | |
| `detect-private-key` | (no project script) | | - | |
| `mixed-line-ending` | (no project script) | | - | |
| `black` | (no project script) | | - | |
| `isort` | (no project script) | | - | |
| `ruff` | (no project script) | | - | |
| `enforce-standards` | `scripts/enforce_standards.py` | | YES | enhanced-cicd-pipeline.yml, quality-checks.yml |
| `no-emoji` | `scripts/check_no_emoji.py` | | **YES (new)** | guards.yml |
| `review-js-parses` | `tools/check_review_js.py` | | **YES (new)** | guards.yml |
| `check-pyc-files` | (no project script) | | - | |
| `check-pygame-dir` | (no project script) | | - | |
| `style-guide-reminder` | `scripts/check_style_guide.py` | | NO | **WAIVED** |
| `dq-index-check` | `scripts/generate_dq_index.py` | `--check` | **YES (new)** | guards.yml |
| `adr-index-check` | `scripts/generate_adr_index.py` | `--check` | **YES (new)** | guards.yml |
| `tools-index-check` | `scripts/generate_tools_index.py` | `--check` | **YES (new)** | guards.yml |
| `action-taxonomy-index-check` | `scripts/generate_action_taxonomy.py` | `--check-stale` | **YES (new)** | guards.yml |
| `credits-json-check` | `scripts/generate_credits.py` | `--check` | **YES (new)** | guards.yml |
| `commitment-calendar-check` | `scripts/generate_commitment_calendar.py` | `--check` | **YES (new)** | guards.yml |
| `class-cache-check` | `tools/check_class_cache.py` | | NO | **WAIVED** |
| `rulings-index-check` | `scripts/generate_rulings.py` | `--check` | **YES (new)** | guards.yml |
| `balance-key-census` | `tools/check_balance_keys.py` | `--check` | **YES (new)** | guards.yml |
| `trust-declaration-check` | `tools/generate_trust_declaration.py` | `--check` | **YES (new)** | guards.yml |
| `credential-check` | `tools/assets/check_credentials.py` | | **YES (new)** | guards.yml |
| `provenance-check` | `tools/assets/check_provenance.py` | | YES | quality-checks.yml |
| `scene-nav-check` | `tools/check_scene_nav.py` | | YES | guards.yml, quality-checks.yml |
| `refusal-classification-check` | `tools/check_refusal_classification.py` | | YES | quality-checks.yml |
| `font-size-ssot-check` | `tools/check_font_sizes.py` | | **YES (new)** | guards.yml |
| `version-sync-check` | `tools/sync_version.py` | `--check` | YES | quality-checks.yml |
| `changelog-structure-check` | `scripts/check_release_notes.py` | | YES | enhanced-release.yml, pre-release-checks.yml |
| `release-index-check` | `scripts/generate_release_metadata.py` | `--check` | **PARTIAL** | enhanced-release.yml |

Before this branch: `13 with no CI presence, 2 waived` -- the fifteen #1265 names.
After: `0 with no CI presence`. `check_guard_parity.py --check` fails if that ever
regresses, and also fails on a **stale waiver** (a waived hook that later gains a CI
presence), so the waiver list can only shrink.

### The two waivers, and why they are not gaps

- **`class-cache-check`** -- CI is structurally blind to the bug. A stale
  `godot/.godot` cache only exists in a long-lived working copy; CI clones fresh and
  always builds a correct one, so the guard would be watching the one place that is
  never wrong. It is also a post-merge/post-checkout hook, not a pre-commit one. What
  CI proves instead is that the DETECTOR still returns both answers --
  `quality-checks.yml` already runs `python -m unittest tests.test_check_class_cache`
  blocking.
- **`style-guide-reminder`** -- not a gate. `scripts/check_style_guide.py` reads
  `git diff --cached`, which is empty on a CI checkout, and without `--strict` it only
  warns. In CI it could return exactly one answer, forever. Wiring it as-is would
  manufacture a green light. #1297 section 3.

## 2. The new workflow

`.github/workflows/guards.yml`, one new file. **No existing workflow is edited** --
they are contended this week, and a guard that cannot be added without a merge conflict
is a guard that does not get added. `.pre-commit-config.yaml` is also untouched, so
there is no conflict with whoever is editing it.

- Triggers: `pull_request` and `push` on `main`, plus `workflow_dispatch` for the reason
  `quality-checks.yml` already learned -- a PR touching `.github/workflows/` can have
  its `pull_request` runs suppressed, and this PR is one of those.
- `permissions: contents: read`, stated with its reasoning, per the comment at the top
  of `release-reminder.yml`. The default token scope is a repo/org setting, so an
  unstated block means the job's authority is whatever someone last set elsewhere and
  can widen without this file changing. These guards only read the checkout.

**Exit-code discipline, which is the part worth reviewing closely:**

- `set +e` first. GitHub's default shell here is `bash -e -o pipefail`, so without it
  the job would stop at the first failing guard and hide the rest. A census that reports
  one finding is not a census.
- `code=${PIPESTATUS[0]}`, never `$?`. After the `| tee` pipeline `$?` is *tee's* status.
  Measured, not assumed:

  ```
  $ bash -c 'exit 7' 2>&1 | tee /dev/null ; echo "naive=$?"
  naive=0
  ```

- **Three outcomes, not two.** `0` pass, `1` measured failure, `2` COULD NOT MEASURE.
  Exit 2 fails the job -- a guard that did not run is not a pass -- but it is annotated
  and summarised as *"no result, not a finding"*, because collapsing it into FAIL
  asserts a result from a run that established nothing.

Driven with fake guards returning 0/1/2 through the real function text extracted from
the workflow:

```
| PASS | zero | ... |
| FAIL (exit 1) | one | ... |
| COULD NOT MEASURE (exit 2) | two | ... |
JOB_EXIT=1        (and all three ::group:: blocks ran -- no -e leak)
```

**All 21 guard invocations, extracted from `guards.yml` itself rather than retyped and
run against this branch, exit 0** -- locally, and then in CI: run
[32681891646](https://github.com/PipFoweraker/pdoom1/actions/runs/32681891646), green
in 29s. Quality Checks and Self-Merge Eligibility are also green on this branch, so
nothing here disturbed the existing gates.

## 3. Self-tests

Three guards had none. Each new `--self-test` was then shown capable of returning the
*other* answer by breaking the detector in-memory and watching it go red -- six
independent breakages, none of which leaves the self-test green:

| guard | breakage | self-test |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `check_scene_nav.py` | `BANNED_RE` neutered | RED |
| `check_scene_nav.py` | `SANCTIONED` widened to a directory | RED |
| `check_no_emoji.py` | `is_emoji` always False | RED |
| `check_no_emoji.py` | decoded-JSON scan neutered (the #1163 blind spot) | RED |
| `check_balance_keys.py` | `is_composed` always True | RED |
| `check_guard_parity.py` | (self-tested against real config; `presence()` cases synthetic) | -- |

Why these three, out of the census:

- **`tools/check_scene_nav.py`** -- blocking in pre-commit AND `quality-checks.yml`
  since the v0.11.0 release-only segfault, and in all that time it has only ever printed
  nothing and exited 0. Its third case is **real code, not a fixture**:
  `godot/autoload/scene_transition.gd` genuinely makes two raw navigation calls, so
  `scan_text` must flag them and `scan_file` must exempt them. That makes the exemption
  provably load-bearing; widening it turns the test red.
- **`tools/check_balance_keys.py`** -- the worked example from the brief, and the only
  gate pointed at the balance surface in either direction. It pins the bug its own
  docstring records: direction 1 must still catch `doom.streams.upgrade_cat_alarm` when
  `doom.streams.` is declared dynamic. The first draft of that file got this wrong and
  reported "no live silent fallbacks" three lines from the sighting it was built for.
  A suppressed gate and a satisfied gate print the same line.
- **`scripts/check_no_emoji.py`** -- this gate exists *because* its predecessor could
  only ever return one answer in practice (the non-blocking handling in
  `enforce_standards.py` let a coffee emoji ship). The self-test pins U+2615 and the
  #1163 mojibake: pure-ASCII BYTES decoding to `U+00E2 U+2020 U+2019`, which the byte
  scanner must NOT see and the decoded-JSON scanner must. That case shipped mojibake to
  players for weeks while this script printed "OK: godot .gd/.json are pure ASCII".

Refactors were kept to the minimum the tests needed: `scan_text()` split out of
`scan_file()`; `adjudicate()` split out of `main()` (byte-identical census output before
and after); `_rel()` made tolerant of a path outside the repo.

Guards still wired with no self-test, in value order, are listed in **#1297 section 4**:
`sync_version.py --check` (documented FATAL, never observed red), `check_font_sizes.py`
(a ratchet whose failing direction has never been exercised), `check_review_js.py`
(exits 0 SKIPPED without node, so on such a machine it is indistinguishable from a
pass), and the five index generators.

## 4. Added on top: the environments guard

From a defect found today across two repos in this estate.

> **AN ENVIRONMENT THAT NO WORKFLOW REFERENCES IS EITHER CLUTTER OR A LIE, AND WHICH
> ONE DEPENDS ENTIRELY ON WHAT IT IS CALLED.**

pdoom1-website has `production-approval`, created 2025-10-09, `protection_rules: []`,
referenced by no workflow. Its NAME asserts an approval gate; it gates nothing. That is
manufactured confidence implemented in a name rather than in code -- one layer below
where anybody looks for it. No file contains the false claim; the repository settings do.

pdoom1 has the same shape, milder. `gh api repos/PipFoweraker/pdoom1/environments`
returns exactly one environment, `copilot`, `protection_rules: []`, created
2025-07-31, and `grep -rn "environment:" .github/workflows/` returns nothing. `copilot`
asserts nothing about safety, so it misleads nobody: clutter, not a lie.

`tools/check_environments.py` diffs the API list against the workflows and classifies
each unreferenced environment by a safety vocabulary (approval / review / gate /
protected / prod / production / sign-off). Both answers, measured:

```
$ python tools/check_environments.py
[environments] PipFoweraker/pdoom1 -- 1 environment(s), 0 referenced by a workflow
  CLUTTER     copilot        protection_rules=0  created 2025-07-31T05:33:30Z
[environments] OK: 1 unreferenced environment(s), none asserting a gate.
                                                                            -> exit 0

$ python tools/check_environments.py --repo PipFoweraker/pdoom1-website
  FINDING     production-approval  protection_rules=0  created 2025-10-09T07:48:31Z
  ... and two more
                                                                            -> exit 1
```

- **It reports only.** It never deletes or edits an environment; settings are Pip's.
- **CI-only, not pre-commit.** A hook that makes a network call is slow and fails
  offline, which teaches people to skip hooks.
- **It emits UNKNOWN (exit 2), never a pass, when it cannot reach GitHub** -- and its
  self-test proves that path is reachable by calling a repo that cannot exist. An
  environments audit that reports "no findings" because it could not look has
  implemented the very defect it exists to detect.
- Matching is by token PREFIX, not substring, so `production` matches `prod` and
  `reproduction-tests` does not. That false positive is pinned in the self-test.
- The self-test uses a synthetic environment list, never live API state -- live state
  changes, and a self-test that reads it is a second copy of the thing being tested.

`GITHUB_TOKEN` with `contents: read` **does** reach the environments endpoint --
measured, not assumed: run
[32681891646](https://github.com/PipFoweraker/pdoom1/actions/runs/32681891646) logs
`[environments] PipFoweraker/pdoom1 -- 1 environment(s), 0 referenced by a workflow`.
Had it 403'd, the guard would have exited 2 (COULD NOT MEASURE), which is the correct
answer and a one-line permissions fix rather than a silent pass; the comment at the
call site says so.

## Scope left, deliberately -- #1297

Not silent truncation; each item has the measurement that justified leaving it.

1. **The formatter/whitespace family** (black / isort / ruff / whitespace hooks) runs on
   changed files only in pre-commit and nowhere in CI. Not wired because whole-tree it
   arrives RED: measured 2026-08-24 over 236 Python files with the pinned versions,
   black would reformat 83, isort reports 78, ruff 178 errors. The wireable shape is
   changed-files-only.
2. **`release-index-check`** -- the PARTIAL above, and `--check` is red on main today
   (`public/releases` says v0.14.0; v0.14.2 is tagged). Regenerate the feed, then promote
   PARTIAL to a failure -- the comment marking that spot is in the file.
3. **`style-guide-reminder`** -- make it gateable or retire it.
4. **Four guards still without a self-test.**
5. **`quality-checks.yml`'s non-blocking steps** -- two `|| echo "WARNING"` gates, one
   `|| echo "INFO"` over `unittest discover tests` (which is why four `tests/test_*.py`
   for guards in this census prove nothing in CI), and an "ASCII Compliance Check" whose
   `if [ $? -ne 0 ]` block is unreachable under `bash -e`. **Not touched on purpose**:
   this PR edits no existing workflow.

## Conflicts

None expected. `.pre-commit-config.yaml` is not modified. The only shared files touched
are the three GENERATED indexes that any commit adding a tool must regenerate
(`docs/TOOLS.md`, `docs/rulings/*`, `docs/calendar/*`); if another lane lands a tool
first, regenerate and re-commit.

Ladder-Impact: none -- no file under `godot/` is touched; CI wiring, tooling and
generated indexes only.

issues.title: fix(release,ui): four player-facing places where "could not tell" read as "fine"
issues.body:
Fixes the four **player-facing** instances of the "manufactured confidence" defect Pip ruled on 2026-08-23: a value meaning "I could not tell" rendered as a value meaning "fine". The 2026-08-24 sweep found 21; these are the ones that reach players.

Every finding was re-verified against the source before being touched. **Two of the sweep's supporting claims did not survive that** and are corrected below.

## F1 + F2 -- `scripts/generate_release_metadata.py`

`extract_changelog_for_version()` returned `Release vX.Y.Z / See CHANGELOG.md for details.` when a version had no CHANGELOG section, and `...No changelog available.` when `CHANGELOG.md` was missing. Both land in the `changelog` field of `public/releases/<tag>.json` **and** the `<description>` of every item in `public/releases/releases.rss` -- deployed, player-visible. Neither is distinguishable from a real, terse release note.

Verified on this tree:

```
$ grep -c "0\.14\.2" CHANGELOG.md
0
$ grep -o "<description>Release v0.13.1" public/releases/releases.rss
<description>Release v0.13.1
```

14 of the 23 entries in the tracked index carry the placeholder.

**Fix.** The function returns `None` -- a sentinel, never prose. Callers treat it as fatal: `generate_all_metadata()` reports every gap, `main()` exits 1. JSON now carries `"changelog": null` plus `"changelog_status": "missing"`; the RSS `<description>` states the absence explicitly rather than standing in for a note.

`--check` now inspects the changelog **field**, not just the tag list and `latest_version`. It could previously call an index "fresh" by every assertion it made while every entry said "See CHANGELOG.md for details."

**Why a pin and not a bare hard-fail.** 15 of 25 tags had no section. A gate red on arrival gets disabled inside a week -- the failure mode this repo already records against `action-taxonomy-index-check`. `scripts/changelog_gap_pin.txt` grandfathers the 14 historical ones as a **shrink-only ratchet**, and they are still printed on every run, so they cannot go quiet. **v0.14.2 is deliberately NOT pinned** -- it is a current release, so the generator stays loud. A test fails if someone silences it.

**Teeth worth naming.** `enhanced-release.yml:239` runs this generator in the `generate-feeds` job that `create-github-release` depends on. A release cut without a CHANGELOG section now **fails the release** instead of publishing a placeholder.

**A third copy, found while tracing callers.** `scripts/generate_release_manifest.py::extract_highlights()` fed the same placeholder into a client tooltip, and would have raised `AttributeError` on `.strip()` once the sentinel landed. Fixed the same way. This was not in the sweep.

## F17 -- `.github/workflows/pre-release-checks.yml`

`grep -q "$TAG_VERSION" CHANGELOG.md` was unanchored and unbracketed, so any mention of the bare string anywhere in 1800+ lines satisfied it -- and it owned the reassuring `SUCCESS CHANGELOG.md contains version X` message. Now `grep -q "^## \[$TAG_VERSION\]"`, the same question the real extractor asks.

**Not cosmetic.** Run over the repo's own 25 tags, 6 passed the old gate with no section heading at all:

| tag | old (unanchored) | anchored |
|---|---|---|
| v0.9.0, v0.10.1, v0.10.2, v0.10.3, v0.11.0, v0.13.1 | PASS | fail |

Those are precisely the releases whose feed entries carried the placeholder. A test runs both forms over the real `CHANGELOG.md` and asserts they never disagree.

**Nuance the sweep did not mention:** `pre-release-checks.yml` also runs `scripts/check_release_notes.py --version`, which raises fatal `RN000` when no section is found. So the loose grep was a *redundant weaker* gate rather than the only one -- its practical blast radius was the false SUCCESS line, not an unguarded release. The fix stands regardless: two gates asking different questions is how the loosest one ends up owning the reassuring message.

## F3 -- `godot/scripts/ui/whats_new_modal.gd`

Three distinct conditions (file missing / unparseable JSON / no entry for this version) collapsed into one sentence: *"No detailed patch notes available for this version."* Only the third makes it true; the other two mean the **build** is broken.

Added a `LoadStatus` enum recording which of five things happened (`BAD_SHAPE` is new -- valid JSON that is not an object with a `versions` array would otherwise assign into a typed Dictionary and blow up). Logs name the cause. Player-facing text stays gentle but no longer claims there are no notes when the notes could not be read.

**The expensive half.** `mark_patch_notes_seen()` ran on the fallback path unconditionally. `has_unseen_patch_notes()` is an inequality against `last_seen_version`, so a build shipped without the data file **silently consumed the player's one showing** -- no second chance at the real notes, ever, for that version. Now marked seen only when notes were actually shown, or when the data loaded fine and genuinely has no entry.

**Build-time gate:** `tools/check_patch_notes.py`, wired into pre-commit on `version.txt` / `patch_notes.json` / the tool itself.

> **CORRECTION to the sweep.** It claimed `patch_notes` appears in zero `.py` and zero `.yml` files, and that nothing checks `patch_notes.json` against `version.txt`. Both are overstated. `patch_notes` appears in `tools/check_ladder_bump.py` and `tests/test_check_ladder_bump.py` (as a path-classification string), and **`godot/tests/unit/test_patch_notes.gd` already asserts the shipped version has an entry**. The real gap is the **tier**: that assertion needs a Godot binary and an import pass, so nothing ran it at commit time. The new tool is a Python mirror of the same assertions and says so in its docstring rather than claiming to be novel.

## Structural finding -- filed separately, NOT fixed here

`pre-release-checks.yml` and `enhanced-release.yml` are **independent workflows both triggered on `push: tags`**, with no dependency between them. A red pre-release check therefore cannot stop publication -- the release builds and publishes in parallel regardless. Filed as its own issue; see the link in the comments.

## Tests

| file | count | covers |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/test_generate_release_metadata.py` | 23 | sentinel contract, null/status fields, RSS absence marker, pin-as-ratchet, `--check` red on placeholders and unpinned nulls / green on a good index, the manifest caller, two-gate agreement |
| `tests/test_check_patch_notes.py` | 13 | fixture-driven red paths; real tree currently clean |
| `godot/tests/unit/test_whats_new_fallback.gd` | 12 | three causes staying three causes, `should_mark_seen` truth table, actual fallback strings |

**Measured, not asserted** -- the new gate driven to red and back on the real tree:

```
$ printf '9.9.9\n' > version.txt && python tools/check_patch_notes.py --quiet
[patch-notes] FAIL:
  - no entry for the shipped version 9.9.9 in patch_notes.json
RED_EXIT=1
$ # restored
GREEN_EXIT=0
```

**Godot fast gate** (`tools/check_class_cache.py --repair` then `python scripts/run_godot_tests.py --quick --ci-mode --min-tests 300`):

```
[PASS] 'quick': 1483 tests, 0 failures, 145/145 files collected, 104s.
[TOTALS] quick: 1483 tests, 0 fail (ok)
```

## Caveat worth stating

**No CI workflow runs pytest.** `grep -rn pytest .github/workflows/` matches only a comment. `tests/` currently has 61 collection errors and 57 failures on `main`, from dead pygame-era modules importing a `src/` package that no longer exists (`src/` is absent from the repo). None involve files touched here -- verified by grepping the failure list for every path in this diff (empty). The Python tests added here are therefore **proof-on-demand, not an automated gate**; the automated gates in this PR are the two pre-commit hooks and the GUT file.

## Follow-up for Pip (blocked on you, deliberately)

`v0.14.2` has no `## [0.14.2]` section in `CHANGELOG.md`, so the generator now exits 1 on it and the tracked feed index is stale (it is missing v0.14.1 and v0.14.2 -- `--check` was already red on `main` before this PR; the hook is scoped to `public/releases/**` so it never fired). Writing those release notes requires authoring real prose about a shipped build, which this PR deliberately does not do -- inventing it is the false-delivery-claim failure #1165 exists to prevent. Once the section exists, `python scripts/generate_release_metadata.py` will regenerate the feed cleanly.

Ladder-Impact: none -- the only `godot/` changes are `godot/scripts/ui/` and `godot/tests/`, both cosmetic surfaces under `check_ladder_bump.py`'s own classification. No gameplay, economy, balance or replay surface touched.

Do NOT merge without review.

issues.title: Release: pre-release-checks.yml cannot block enhanced-release.yml (independent workflows, same tag trigger)
issues.body:
## A red pre-release check cannot stop a release

`.github/workflows/pre-release-checks.yml` and `.github/workflows/enhanced-release.yml` are **two independent workflows with the same trigger**:

```yaml
# pre-release-checks.yml
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*.*.*'
```

```yaml
# enhanced-release.yml
on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*.*.*'
  workflow_dispatch:
    ...
```

GitHub Actions has no cross-workflow `needs:`. Pushing a tag starts **both at once**, and nothing in `enhanced-release.yml` waits on, queries, or is gated by the outcome of `pre-release-checks.yml`. So every gate in the pre-release workflow -- the CHANGELOG section check, the `check_release_notes.py` structure and citation guards, the `project.godot` version match, the clean-tree check -- can go **red while the release builds, publishes, and uploads assets in parallel**.

## Why this matters more than it looks

The workflow's own name and its failure handler both imply blocking. On failure it opens an issue titled `Pre-Release Checks Failed: <tag>` whose body says:

> Fix these issues and re-tag the release.

By the time anyone reads that, the release may already be published. The remediation advice describes a gate that does not exist.

`enhanced-release.yml` does carry its own internal gate (`Guard the release body against false delivery claims`, #1165), which sits between assembly and publication *within* that workflow and is genuinely blocking. That one works. The point here is that the **pre-release workflow's** checks are advisory in practice while presenting as blocking.

## Evidence

- Both files, `on.push.tags` blocks quoted above.
- No `needs:`, `workflow_run`, `workflow_call`, or repository-dispatch link between them.
- `enhanced-release.yml`'s job graph (`validate-data`, `build-godot`, `generate-feeds`, `create-release-manifest`, `create-github-release`) references only jobs inside its own file.

## Options, roughly in increasing order of intrusiveness

1. **Fold the pre-release steps into `enhanced-release.yml`** as a first job that every other job `needs:`. Single workflow, real ordering, one place to read. Costs the ability to run the checks standalone via `workflow_dispatch` unless a separate thin caller is kept.
2. **Convert `pre-release-checks.yml` to a reusable workflow** (`on: workflow_call`) and have `enhanced-release.yml` call it as a gating job. Keeps the file boundary and the standalone dispatch path; adds one layer of indirection.
3. **Leave the split and remove the implication.** Rename to something advisory, and fix the auto-filed issue body so it does not tell people to "re-tag" as though publication had been prevented. Cheapest, but leaves the checks toothless.

My read: option 2 preserves what the split was presumably for (running the checks by hand against a candidate) while making the tag path actually gated. But this is a release-process call, not a code call, so it wants a ruling rather than a patch.

## Provenance

Found while fixing the unanchored CHANGELOG grep in `pre-release-checks.yml` (PR #1298, finding F17 of the 2026-08-24 manufactured-confidence sweep). Deliberately **not** fixed there -- that PR scoped itself to the four player-facing string defects, and restructuring the release trigger graph is a different decision with different risk.

Not verified: whether any past release actually published while these checks were red. Establishing that needs a pass over Actions history for the tag pushes, which I did not do. UNKNOWN.

issues.title: guards: the five things #1265 deliberately left, with the measurements that justified leaving them
issues.body:
Follow-up to #1265. PR "guards: thirteen that ran nowhere but pre-commit" closed the
gap the issue names -- `python tools/check_guard_parity.py --check` now reports
`0 with no CI presence` -- and deliberately left five things out. This issue is the
explicit list, so the deferral is not silent truncation.

## 1. The formatter / whitespace family runs on changed files only, and nowhere in CI

`black`, `isort`, `ruff`, `trailing-whitespace`, `end-of-file-fixer`,
`mixed-line-ending`, `check-added-large-files`, `detect-private-key`,
`check-merge-conflict`, `check-case-conflict`, `check-yaml`, `check-json` are all
third-party hooks. `grep -rniE "black|isort|ruff" .github/workflows/` returns nothing,
so `--no-verify` or an uninstalled pre-commit steps over every one of them.

They were NOT wired, and the reason is a measurement, not a judgement. On 2026-08-24,
over the 236 Python files under `scripts/ tools/ tests/ docs/` (excluding
`archive/`/`legacy/`), with the exact versions pinned in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`
(black 24.1.1, isort 5.13.2, ruff 0.1.15):

| tool | whole-tree result |
| --- | --- |
| `black --check --line-length=100` | 83 files would be reformatted |
| `isort --check-only --profile=black --line-length=100` | 78 files incorrectly sorted |
| `ruff check` | 178 errors (57 auto-fixable) |

A whole-tree CI gate would therefore arrive RED, and this repo already records what
happens next -- see the `action-taxonomy-index-check` comment in
`.pre-commit-config.yaml`: "a gate that is red on arrival gets disabled inside a week".

Reproduce:

```
python -m venv /tmp/fmt && /tmp/fmt/bin/pip install black==24.1.1 isort==5.13.2 ruff==0.1.15
files=$(find scripts tools tests docs -name '*.py' -not -path '*/archive/*' -not -path '*/legacy/*')
/tmp/fmt/bin/python -m black --check --line-length=100 $files
/tmp/fmt/bin/python -m isort --check-only --profile=black --line-length=100 $files
/tmp/fmt/bin/python -m ruff check $files
```

**The wireable shape is changed-files-only**, matching what pre-commit actually does:
`git diff --name-only origin/$BASE_REF...HEAD -- '*.py'` piped into the three tools.
That closes the `--no-verify` bypass without demanding a 236-file cleanup first. The
alternative is one large formatting commit and then a whole-tree gate; that is a
bigger, more conflict-prone change and belongs on its own.

## 2. `release-index-check` is PARTIAL, and it is RED on main today

`scripts/generate_release_metadata.py` DOES appear in `enhanced-release.yml` -- as
`--version "$VERSION"`, which REGENERATES the feed. The pre-commit hook runs `--check`,
which GATES it. Grepping the filename reports "covered"; the gate is not covered at all.
`tools/check_guard_parity.py` reports this as PARTIAL rather than YES for exactly this
reason, and it is the subtlety a naive census misses.

It was not wired because it does not pass:

```
$ python scripts/generate_release_metadata.py --check
  - latest_version is 'v0.14.0', expected 'v0.14.2'
[check] Fix: python scripts/generate_release_metadata.py
```

`public/releases/` is two tags behind (`git tag --sort=-v:refname | head -3` gives
v0.14.2, v0.14.1, v0.14.0). So: regenerate the feed, commit it, then promote PARTIAL
from a report to a failure in `check_guard_parity.main()` -- the comment marking that
spot is already in the file.

## 3. `style-guide-reminder` cannot go red

`scripts/check_style_guide.py` reads `git diff --cached`, which is empty on a CI
checkout, and without `--strict` it only warns. In CI it would return exactly one
answer, forever -- a manufactured green. It carries a WAIVER in
`tools/check_guard_parity.py` saying so. Either make it gateable (a `--base REF` mode
that diffs a range instead of the index, run with `--strict`) or retire it. Leaving a
hook that cannot fail is the thing #1265 is against.

## 4. Guards still wired with no self-test

#1265's act 2 asked for self-tests on wired gates. Three were added
(`check_scene_nav.py`, `check_balance_keys.py`, `scripts/check_no_emoji.py`), plus two
on the new tools. Still without one, roughly in value order:

- `tools/sync_version.py --check` -- blocking in `quality-checks.yml`, documented as
  FATAL (a silent drift forks the leaderboard board key). Never observed red.
- `tools/check_font_sizes.py` -- a RATCHET. A ratchet whose failing direction has never
  been exercised is a counter, not a gate.
- `tools/check_review_js.py` -- exits 0 with SKIPPED when `node` is absent, so on a
  machine without node it is indistinguishable from a pass. Worth pinning that the
  SKIPPED path is reported and that a broken JS fixture really fails.
- `tools/generate_trust_declaration.py --check` and the five index generators
  (`generate_dq_index` / `generate_adr_index` / `generate_tools_index` /
  `generate_credits` / `generate_rulings`). These are cheaper cases -- a stale-index
  check is nearly self-proving, since regenerating and re-running exercises both
  answers -- but none has a command that demonstrates it.

## 5. Non-blocking steps in `quality-checks.yml` (do not edit it in a contended week)

Not touched, because that file is contended and this PR deliberately edits no existing
workflow. Recorded so it is not lost:

- `python scripts/enforce_standards.py --check-all || echo "WARNING ..."` -- the `||`
  makes it advisory. Same shape as the `|| true` #1178 removed elsewhere.
- `python scripts/ci_health_integration.py --gate-check || echo "WARNING ..."` -- same.
- The "ASCII Compliance Check" step runs `python scripts/intelligent_ascii_converter.py
  --dry-run` and then `if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then ... exit 1; fi`. GitHub's default shell is
  `bash -e -o pipefail`, so a non-zero exit aborts the step BEFORE the `if` is reached:
  that `if` block is unreachable code, and the step's real behaviour comes from `-e`.
  It works by accident, which is a different thing from working.
- `python -m unittest discover tests || echo "INFO: ..."` in
  `enhanced-cicd-pipeline.yml` swallows every failure in `tests/`, which is why
  `tests/test_check_credentials.py`, `tests/test_generate_tools_index.py`,
  `tests/test_generate_commitment_calendar.py` and
  `tests/test_generate_action_taxonomy.py` exist and prove nothing in CI. The pattern
  `quality-checks.yml` already uses for two of these -- naming the module blocking --
  is the fix.

issues.title: docs: release security -- the hole was already closed, and the command that said otherwise could never have said so
issues.body:
**A proposal document, not a change.** No repository setting, ruleset,
environment, secret or permission was created, changed or deleted. Section 7
carries the exact commands to apply each option and states, before the first
one, that none has been run. Those are Pip's to run.

Adds `docs/deployment/RELEASE_SECURITY_2026-08-24.md` (979 lines). The calendar
index is regenerated because the doc carries its measurement date.

## The brief was already out of date, and the command that said so could never have said so

The brief was written from a measurement reading *"one ruleset, target branch,
enforcement DISABLED; no tag protection; anyone with push access can publish a
public release."* Re-running the commands found a **second ruleset that did not
exist when that measurement was taken**:

```
$ gh api repos/PipFoweraker/pdoom1/rulesets --jq '.[] | "\(.name) | enforcement=\(.enforcement) | target=\(.target) | created=\(.created_at)"'
Default no-ruin rules | enforcement=disabled | target=branch | created=2025-08-20T19:54:01.556+10:00
Release tags: v* created by admins only, never moved, never deleted | enforcement=active | target=tag | created=2026-08-24T11:17:43.875+10:00
```

Rules `creation` / `deletion` / `non_fast_forward` on `refs/tags/v*`, one bypass
actor (repository role `5` = admin). **The primary hole the document was
commissioned to propose a fix for is closed.**

**The methodological finding outranks that.** One of the three briefed commands
was `gh api repos/PipFoweraker/pdoom1/tags/protection`, and its 404 was read as
evidence of absence. That endpoint is the **legacy tag-protection-rules API**,
which rulesets superseded; it returns 404 against a repository with a fully
active tag ruleset -- which is exactly what this repository was doing at the
moment it was run. **The command cannot return the other answer, so it was never
evidence.** That is `CLAUDE.md`'s own claim-audit amendment, applied to the brief
that cited it.

## Requested explicitly: the supply-chain check is CLEAN

Recording it as such, because a clean finding is worth as much as a dirty one.

```
$ grep -rn "pull_request_target" .github/     -> no output
$ grep -rn "workflow_run" .github/workflows/  -> no output
$ grep -rn "issue_comment:" .github/workflows/ -> no output
```

Zero occurrences across all 16 workflows. Stronger version of the same check:
every workflow referencing a non-`GITHUB_TOKEN` secret (`CROSS_REPO_TOKEN`,
`WEBSITE_SYNC_TOKEN`) is triggered by push-to-main, schedule, release or
`workflow_call` -- **never** by `pull_request`. The seven `pull_request`
workflows reference nothing beyond `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Untrusted code and secrets
are cleanly separated. Somebody also already knew about `${{ }}` script
injection: the `github-script` step passes the tag name via `process.env` with
the reason written next to it.

## What IS protected (an honest picture, not an alarm)

`main` requires 1 approval, dismisses stale reviews, requires last-push approval
and three status checks, forbids force-push and deletion, requires linear
history and conversation resolution. Default `GITHUB_TOKEN` is read-only. No
deploy keys. That is a well-configured branch.

## What is not -- four of these were not in the brief

- **`enforce_admins: false`, `required_signatures: false`.** Every rule above is
  advisory for Pip, which matters because far more machinery on this box acts as
  Pip than there are third parties with write access.
- **Three collaborators, not one.** `PipFoweraker` (admin), `tegabeta` and
  `stevenhobartwork-create` (write). The call did not 403.
- **`workflow_dispatch` on `enhanced-release.yml` is open to write access** and
  the tag ruleset does not gate it. It also, **predicted-not-tested**, likely
  *broke* the emergency dispatch path: `action-gh-release` publishes as
  `github-actions[bot]`, which holds no repository role and is not a bypass
  actor. Section 7.1 has the cheap check. Finding this out on the night of a
  hotpatch is the expensive way.
- **93 `uses:` references, ZERO SHA-pinned**, `allowed_actions: "all"`. Two
  mutable third-party tags run inside the job that publishes, holding
  `contents: write`, in a call tree that inherits `CROSS_REPO_TOKEN`.
- **Five `DH_*` secrets, one an SSH private key, with zero references** in any
  workflow.
- **`Default no-ruin rules`**: created and last touched 16 seconds apart in
  August 2025, never enforced, both rules already delivered by branch
  protection. Present, reassuringly named, doing nothing.

## The integrity chain, described more precisely than it has been

- The **freshness marker** proves the pack was built from the current working
  tree. It is **not an integrity control** -- generated locally, checked locally,
  deleted, never published. It answers "did my source reach the pack?", never
  "did this pack reach the player unaltered?"
- The **manifest sha256** proves the zip is byte-for-byte what was uploaded. It
  cannot prove **who** uploaded it: a substituted build gets hashed just as
  faithfully. That gap is what signing closes.

Two corrections to existing docs, both in the direction that flatters us less:

- `docs/design/UPDATER_DESIGN.md:179-182` still states the pre-#1069 limitation
  as current; CI now routes through the proven builder.
- `docs/release/CODE_SIGNING.md:196` says `sign_release.py` "is tested against
  its three states" -- **there is no test file**. The #1282 commit message is
  accurate where the doc is not ("All three states verified" = hand-run once).

Also found: with no `--assets-dir`, `generate_release_manifest.py` publishes a
manifest with **zero integrity anchors and exits 0**. The one silent degradation
in an otherwise fail-loud tool.

## Recommendation, including what to skip

Do the three chores (delete the dead secrets, delete the dead ruleset, SHA-pin
the two third-party actions) -- under an hour, no recurring friction, and the
pinning is the only item addressing the one actor Pip cannot revoke. Verify the
dispatch side effect before needing it. Push code signing **on the SmartScreen
argument, not the tampering argument**: the release notice currently *has to*
train players to dismiss the one OS warning that would catch a substitute, and
that training compounds at this cadence.

**The option not to bother with is the environment with required reviewers.** It
taxes the only path anyone has ever used (all eight releases: tag-push, by Pip);
its unique coverage over the now-active tag ruleset is thin; a stolen admin
session can approve its own deployment, so it misses the dominant threat; and it
adds a release-sitting-unpublished failure mode indistinguishable from a failed
one at 23:00 on a league night. If the pause is wanted, `draft: true` buys the
same pause as a **reviewed code change** rather than an invisible setting.

## Verification

- All five bracketed hedges say what would settle them.
- Appendix lists every command used; all read-only.
- `generate_commitment_calendar.py --check`, `generate_rulings.py --check`,
  `check_no_emoji.py`: pass. Full pre-commit run passed in the foreground.
- Doc is 0 non-ASCII bytes, 0 CRLF.

`Ladder-Impact: none -- documentation only.`

issues.title: fix(leaderboard-api): encode before truncating, and cut names on codepoint boundaries (#1272)
issues.body:
Closes #1272.

## The issue's diagnosis holds, and it was missing the half that makes it fire

`score_api.php:139` did `ftruncate($fp, 0); rewind($fp); fwrite($fp, json_encode($entries));`.
`json_encode()` evaluates as an argument, so it runs **after** the truncate.
It returns `false` on malformed UTF-8, and `fwrite($fp, false)` writes the empty
string. One submitted name emptied the whole league while the API answered
`{"ok":true,"added":true,"rank":N}`. That is exactly what the issue says.

What the issue does not say is **where the malformed UTF-8 came from**. It could
not come from the request body: `json_decode()` rejects malformed input and the
handler bails with `bad json`. It came from line 110, which cut the name with
**byte-wise** `substr($s, 0, 40)`. So the two items in the issue were one
mechanism -- the truncation *generated* the encode failure it then failed to
check for.

## Measured, not inferred

Locally, php 8.3.14:

| claim | result |
| --- | --- |
| `substr(LIVE_FULL_LAB, 0, 40)` reproduces the live board value | `"GRIM (Global Risk Intervention Mechanism"`, bracket eaten |
| 41-byte name whose cut **splits** a codepoint | `json_encode()` -> `false`, `JSON_ERROR_UTF8` |
| 40-byte multibyte name cutting **on** a boundary | encodes fine -- the trigger is the split, not being non-ASCII |
| `fwrite($fp, false)` | returns **`int(0)`, not `false`** |
| end-to-end vs the pre-fix file over `php -S` | 7-row board -> **0 rows**, API answers `ok:true` |

That fourth row matters: a `if (fwrite(...) === false)` check would have missed
this entirely. The new check compares against `strlen($json)`.

## Read-only against the deployed api.pdoom1.com, 2026-08-24

GET only. No POST, no writes, no live data touched.

- The amputated `GRIM (Global Risk Intervention Mechanism` row is still on
  `(weekly-2026-w32, L4)`.
- `GET ?seed=%FF&version=L4&limit=1` returns **HTTP 200 with a zero-byte body**.
  Same missing check on the *read* path -- `$seed` is echoed back unvalidated,
  `json_encode` fails, PHP echoes `false` as `""`. **No token required.**
- **Every board probed returns parseable JSON**, so **no currently stored name
  is invalid UTF-8**. The live boards are *not* one query away from emptying.
  (Stored invalid bytes would make the GET's own `json_encode` fail, i.e. an
  empty body -- none of the seeded boards did that.)

The `%FF` probe also confirms the deployed file matches this repo's pre-fix
version on that line, which partly answers the issue's "the deployed copy's
state is UNKNOWN".

## What changed

1. **Encode before truncating.** An encode failure now returns 500 and leaves
   the board file untouched.
2. **`fit_utf8()`** cuts on a codepoint boundary and appends a visible `...`, so
   a shortened name reads as truncated rather than as a typo. Deliberately
   **not** `mb_substr()` -- mbstring is not guaranteed on Dreamhost shared
   hosting (and is absent from the stock PHP build these tests ran on). It uses
   `preg_match('//u', ...)`, measured to agree with `json_encode()` on all nine
   probe cases.
3. **Short writes restore the previous bytes** instead of leaving a stump.
4. **`load_board()` returns `null` for "unreadable", never `[]`.** POST now
   refuses to overwrite a board it could not parse -- previously a corrupt board
   was silently replaced by a single row, a second data-loss path with the same
   signature.
5. **GET validates `seed`/`version` encoding**, and every response goes through
   `respond()`, so PHP can no longer emit a silent empty body.
6. **`operator_name` added to `$ALLOWED_FIELDS`** (the issue's second item), and
   the POST response now echoes the stored `player_name`.
7. The comment in `godot/scripts/leaderboard.gd` claiming score_api.php "lives on
   the server and is in no repo here" was **false** -- and that belief is why
   this sat unfixed for two weeks. Corrected.

## Tests

`server/leaderboard/tests/test_score_api.php` -- 51 assertions. There was no PHP
test harness in this repo (everything else is GUT or pytest) and PHPUnit for one
file would be more machinery than the file, so this is dependency-free: no
composer, only `pcre` + `json`. It boots `php -S` over a copy of the API in a
temp docroot with a temp data dir and drives real HTTP.

```
php server/leaderboard/tests/test_score_api.php
```
-> `51 assertions, 0 failed / PASS` (exit 0).

**It is shown capable of returning the other answer:**

```
git show origin/main:server/leaderboard/score_api.php > /tmp/old_api.php
PDOOM_SCORE_API=/tmp/old_api.php php server/leaderboard/tests/test_score_api.php
```
-> 9 FAILs, including `expected: 8 / actual: 0` for the board row count, and
`expected: 400 / actual: 200` for the `%FF` GET.

**Three outcomes, not two.** `0` = pass, `1` = measured failure, `2` = DID NOT
COMPLETE. The `2` is not decoration: the pre-fix score_api.php calls `exit()`
when included, and an earlier draft of this harness **returned green having run
23 of its assertions**. That is the same manufactured-confidence defect as the
endpoint's, so the harness now runs end-to-end *before* the include and has a
shutdown guard. Wired into `quality-checks.yml`.

## NOT DEPLOYED -- this is the important caveat

**This repo has no deploy path to api.pdoom1.com.** Merging this changes nothing
a player touches. The fix ships only when someone uploads the file, and the
README now documents the single GET that distinguishes the deployed version from
the repo version without a POST:

```
curl "https://api.pdoom1.com/score_api.php?seed=%FF&version=L4&limit=1"
```

HTTP 200 + zero bytes = still vulnerable. HTTP 400 + JSON error = fix is live.

Two follow-ups deliberately left open: raising the 40-byte limit (a two-repo
change -- the client fits to the same number), and the client sending
`operator_name` as its own key, which must not start until this is deployed or
the operator goes on the wire twice.

Ladder-Impact: none -- server-side API and tests; the only `godot/` edit is a
comment correction in leaderboard.gd with no reachable behaviour change.

Not merged, per instruction.

issues.title: design: the diegetic opening -- nine atoms, nine ladder verdicts, and the one that cannot ship cosmetically
issues.body:
**Design document only. No GDScript. Nothing ruled, nothing built.**

Pip dictated a substantial redesign of the game's opening in voice memos on 2026-08-24 --
atoms M24-002 .. M24-009, stored verbatim in
`coordination/tools/atoms/memo_rulings_2026-08-24.jsonl` and summarised in
`coordination/UNPACK_2026-08-24_morning-memos.md` section D. **Nothing from those memos had
been filed into pdoom1** (checked: `gh issue list --search "M24"` and four other searches
return zero). This writes the direction up against what the repo already contains.

New file: `docs/game-design/DESIGN_2026-08-24_diegetic-opening.md` (977 lines).
The other four changed files are the generated rulings and calendar indexes, regenerated
because the doc carries one `RULING:` declaration and quotes dates in prose.

## What it contains

1. **What exists today**, with file paths and line numbers, no proposals.
2. **The nine atoms one at a time** -- what each means concretely, what it touches, what it
   replaces, and an explicit ladder verdict.
3. **Instants/interrupts** gets its own section: three shapes with trade-offs and a
   recommendation.
4. **What cannot be done without forking**, nine items, each with its `BUILD_VS_LADDER`
   section 3.1 trigger.
5. **Twelve open questions for Pip**, each answerable in one line.
6. **A recommended slice** -- six items, one release, none of them forking.

## What the grounding changed about the brief

The relayed six-item summary was accurate but the repo is further along than it implies:

- **The cold open already shows the strangers who help you up.** `POSTER_ART` is
  `intro_bus_strangers_help.webp` (`cold_open_sequence.gd:99`), described in the source as
  *"the rainy street the traveler lands in ... teleport back, meet a bus."* Keys are what is
  missing, not the scene.
- **The office is already the wallpaper.** `main.tscn:16` draws `office_wide_day.webp` at
  35% modulate under a scrim, in both modes. The persistent-stage problem is narrower than
  it reads: `main_ui.gd:403` registers the whole `WatchScreen`, and therefore `OfficeFloor`,
  as watch-only.
- **Player-initiated pause does not exist.** `screen_mode.gd:98-104` is a `disabled = true`
  stub. M24-006's *"because the sim can now be paused"* is half true -- the world can pause
  it (`month_controller.gd`, `PAUSED_ON_WINDOW`, and it survives save/load), the player
  cannot. Speed control does ship (`_SPEEDS` at `:37`).
- **A base-building toy already runs.** `office_sandbox.gd` v4.1: side-by-side compare view,
  `RenderGrid` placement with footprint occupancy, quality tiers, poster compositing. What
  Aileen cannot be shown is the payoff loop -- ADR-0018 names placement-gated commands as one
  of two forbidden rot modes, with a review clause dated 2027-07-27.
- **Stranded art, measured** over all 503 images under `godot/assets/` (uid + `res://` search
  across 536 files): **151 referenced by nothing, 9.9 MB.** Richest seam is 15 CRT-dossier
  portraits, 5.35 MB, which `patch_notes.json:216` already tells players are on candidate
  cards. The three blockers are structural, not artistic: `slot_picks.json` is `{}`,
  `props_manifest.json` gates every prop, and `event_dialog.gd` has zero
  `texture|sprite|image` matches -- there is no `TextureRect` in it at all.
- **The prior interrupt thinking is in `coordination`, not here**
  (`DESIGN_2026-08-12_interrupt-resolution-variants.md`). Its A/B/C question was never ruled,
  and M24-006 is orthogonal to it -- A/B/C is about the queue, M24-006 is about a second hand
  of cards. The doc cites it rather than re-deriving it.

## The verdicts

**Do not fork:** keys replacing the phone (and bumping `INTRO_VERSION` is explicitly
ladder-neutral per `BUILD_VS_LADDER` 4.2a); the persistent office; the delivery-trolley
animation (ADR-0018 rider b puts render-local effects *outside* the doctrine's scope);
org-type decor (`org_type` is already first-class state at `game_state.gd:205-208` -- the
architecture doc's claim that it is not is stale); a cosmetic instants tray; the alpha
sandbox as an unranked mode; and rendering the stranded art.

**Forks:** any instant with a real sim effect, at any price, on three independent triggers.
That is the one place Pip's stated constraint and his stated want disagree, and the document
says so plainly rather than picking the convenient answer.

## Recommendation, in one line

Ship the persistent office plus a real pause button plus a *cosmetic* instants tray, and hold
the genuine second action class for an epoch cut -- because M24-005's own sentence
(*"Reinforces that some actions are trivial and cost no attention"*) is a claim about feel
that free-because-cosmetic delivers completely and truthfully, and because a real instants
class lands on top of two unruled questions (A/B/C, and #1223's *"what is the Action Queue
once things take time?"*) that would make it a double build.

## Related

Issues #1210, #1202, #1223, #1218, #1141, #1229, #1044, #794, #1134 -- all cited, none
re-opened.

Ladder-Impact: none -- design document only, no code.

issues.title: docs: the ladder epoch was never forecastable, so stop publishing a forecast (#1152)
issues.body:
## What this is

#1152 filed the version -> ladder-epoch cells in `docs/ROADMAP.md` and
`docs/RELEASE_NOMENCLATURE.md` as "off by one from v0.14 down". They are not off
by one. Both tables encode **one ladder epoch per minor version**, and this repo
has never behaved that way -- so correcting the numbers would have re-staled them
by the next mid-version fork.

Re-derived from git history in this tree (`git log -p -- ladder_version.txt`),
not from a summary or another agent's report:

| epoch | date | commit | version at cut | minor bump? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | 2026-07-23 | `e0963ca9` | -- | counter created |
| L2 | 2026-07-24 | `f8c36edf` | 0.13.0 | **yes** |
| L3 | 2026-07-27 | `9abe20a7` | 0.13.1 | no -- mid-version fork |
| L4 | 2026-08-07 | `7368e237` | 0.14.0 | **yes** |
| L5 | 2026-08-21 | `38528c22` | 0.14.2 | no -- a PATCH release forked |
| L6 | 2026-08-23 | `38c5951e` | 0.14.2 | no -- mid-version fork |

Six epochs, four minor versions, three mid-version forks, two of those inside
v0.14.x. `ROADMAP.md` was forecasting **L5 for v0.15 on 4 Sep**; L5 and L6 were
both spent in August.

**Ruling (Pip, 2026-08-24)**, declared in the generator's docstring under flavour
`release-cadence` and now in `docs/rulings/RULINGS.md`:

> A minor version bump ALWAYS cuts the ladder, and the ladder MAY ALSO cut
> mid-version whenever gameplay forks. Therefore ladder epochs >= minor
> versions, always, and the ladder epoch is NEVER forecastable.

## What lands

**`tools/generate_release_horizon.py`** -- GENERATE layer with a `--check` gate,
the same anti-rot pattern as the DQ index, the rulings index and the commitment
calendar. It emits three tiers and keeps them visually apart, because rendering
three kinds of certainty in one typeface is what rotted the tables it replaces:

1. **SCHEDULED** -- monthly train, first Friday, out to v0.20, with the ISO-week
   seed each date implies. Fully generated; nothing here is a judgement call.
2. **FORECAST** -- theme names and headlines. *Not* generated. Still Pip's, still
   hand-maintained in `ROADMAP.md`, now labelled as a forecast.
3. **NOT FORECASTABLE** -- the ladder epoch, emitted only as a **floor that
   ratchets** (`>= L6`) read from `ladder_version.txt`. No version row anywhere
   carries a predicted epoch, and a test asserts that for every generated block.

Outputs: `docs/releases/RELEASE_HORIZON.md`, `docs/releases/release_horizon.json`,
plus a marker-delimited generated region spliced into both published documents.
Wired into `.pre-commit-config.yaml` as `release-horizon-check`.

```
python tools/generate_release_horizon.py --report
python tools/generate_release_horizon.py --check      # pre-commit gate
python tools/generate_release_horizon.py --self-test  # replays real history
```

### The ISO-week trap, pinned

The featured seed names the ISO week the league opens in. **Friday 2027-01-01 --
v0.19's scheduled date -- is in ISO week 53 OF 2026**, so the seed is
`weekly-2026-w53`. A generator formatting `date.year` emits `weekly-2027-w53`, a
week that does not exist. `w1` and `w01` are different board keys, and a board
cannot be tidied after it opens.

`tests/test_generate_release_horizon.py` pins the same boundary cases as
`godot/tests/unit/test_iso_week_seed.gd` (which currently lives on
`release/catch-players-up-0.14.3`, unmerged), **plus** one assertion that the
naive formatting actually differs -- without it every case would pass under the
bug, because it only fires in January.

### `--self-test` returns both answers

It replays every `ladder_version.txt` cut and classifies each: 1 counter
creation, 2 explained by a minor bump, 3 mid-version gameplay forks. A check that
can only return one answer proves nothing. The counts live there and deliberately
**not** in the generated prose, where they would go stale at the next cut.

## Also in here

- **v0.19 lands on New Year's Day.** The tool FLAGS the collision and never moves
  a date; the ruling owed is recorded in `RELEASE_NOMENCLATURE.md`. Good Friday
  is included in the holiday set because it is the one holiday guaranteed to be
  able to *be* a first Friday -- and in April 2026 it was.
- **#1152's second ask.** `L<n>` is overloaded: ladder epoch vs the L0-L3
  distribution update ladder vs L0..L10 build/art lanes. One disambiguating
  section added to `RELEASE_NOMENCLATURE.md`, cross-linked from `GLOSSARY.md`
  (which already carried half of it).
- **Nomenclature corrections.** The rhythm table said an Epoch *is* a Monthly
  Theme; the fork rule said "bump minor + ladder". Both encoded the coupling that
  is false. Fixed, and the shipped epoch history is now stated as measured fact.
- **`scripts/generate_commitment_calendar.py`**: the Monthly Themes table lost
  its Ladder column, so the theme-cell index moves 1 -> 0 (commented). The .ics
  release-train event summaries are unchanged by that; the churn there is line
  numbers plus the new dates this branch's own text mentions.
- **Atom store ruler named at build time**, per atomise protocol clause 3: Pip
  Foweraker, interim. Same shape as `tools/check_release_ledger.py`.

## Verification run against this tree

```
python tools/generate_release_horizon.py --check      -> up to date
python tools/generate_release_horizon.py --self-test  -> PASS, both answers
python -m pytest tests/test_generate_release_horizon.py -q   -> 15 passed
python -m pytest tests/test_generate_commitment_calendar.py tests/test_generate_tools_index.py -q  -> 29 passed
python tools/check_ladder_bump.py --base origin/main --head HEAD  -> OK
pre-commit (full run on commit)                       -> all hooks green
```

`tests/test_ascii_compliance.py` fails 52 tests on this branch **and on clean
`origin/main`** (pre-existing, unrelated docs); subtests passing went 568 -> 570.

Nothing under `godot/` is touched, so the Godot suite was not run.

Closes #1152.
