issues.title: ci: give docs-sync the permission it has never had, so its red means something
issues.body:
Partial fix for #1279. It takes the first two acceptance criteria and leaves the other three open on the issue.

## What was measured, not assumed

`gh run list --workflow=docs-sync.yml --limit 200`, which returns the workflow's
COMPLETE history (127 runs, so the 200 cap never bound):

| event | conclusion | n |
|---|---|---:|
| `pull_request` | failure | **77** |
| `push` (main) | success | **50** |

No other conclusion appears -- no cancelled, no skipped. Oldest run 2025-12-07,
newest 2026-08-22. So the split is not "since 2026-07-28" as #1279 estimated;
**this workflow has never once passed on a PR, in its entire life.** The issue
undercounted because it looked at the last 20 rows.

Reproduce:

```
gh run list --workflow=docs-sync.yml --limit 200 --json conclusion,event,createdAt
```

That command is capable of returning the other answer -- `Godot Tests` run
through the same query comes back mixed, which is what a working check looks
like.

## Root cause, read out of a log

`gh run view 32569928505 --log-failed` prints the token the job was handed:

```
##[group]GITHUB_TOKEN Permissions
Contents: read
Metadata: read
Packages: read
##[endgroup]
```

and then, from the `Comment PR with preview info` step:

```
RequestError [HttpError]: Resource not accessible by integration
  status: 403
  method: 'POST',
  url: 'https://api.github.com/repos/PipFoweraker/pdoom1/issues/1271/comments'
##[error]Unhandled error: HttpError: Resource not accessible by integration
```

The 403 is present in the log of EVERY failed run whose log still exists --
checked 28279393500 (2026-06-27), 30333948301 (2026-07-28), 31645532508
(2026-08-12), 32565864980 and 32569928505 (2026-08-22). Runs older than the
90-day retention return HTTP 410, so the cause before 2026-06-27 is inferred
from the identical config, not proven.

Main is green because `comment-pr` is gated on
`github.event_name == 'pull_request'` and never runs on a push. That is the
whole reason four weeks of red was invisible: the failure lives in a job that
only exists where nobody was looking at the summary.

## The change

Per-job, not workflow-wide:

```yaml
comment-pr:
  permissions:
    contents: read
    pull-requests: write

check-docs-sync:
  permissions:
    contents: read
```

**`pull-requests: write` and not `issues: write`.** Both were candidates,
because `github.rest.issues.createComment` hits the shared issue-comments
endpoint. What settles it is the job's own `if:` -- `comment-pr` runs ONLY on
`pull_request`, so `context.issue.number` is always a PR number and the
resource GitHub authorises is the pull request. `issues: write` would work too
and would additionally grant write access to every real issue in the repo,
which nothing in this workflow needs. Least privilege is the PR scope.

## Three things deliberately NOT done

1. **`contents: write` for the auto-commit step.** `Auto-commit updated docs
   (main branch only)` ends in `git push`, which needs `contents: write` and
   does not have it. It has never fired -- every main run so far found the docs
   already in sync -- so it has never been observed either working or 403ing.
   Granting push-to-main rights on the strength of a step nobody has seen run
   is a bigger call than this repair; it is flagged in a comment above the job
   so the next person makes it knowingly rather than inheriting it.
2. **The chronic-red detector** (`tools/check_chronic_red.py`) that #1279 asks
   for. Not built here.
3. **Extending `scripts/check_no_emoji.py` to `.github/**`.** Not done, but
   here is the survey it needs -- six files under `.github/` carry non-ASCII
   today:

   | file | non-ASCII chars |
   |---|---:|
   | `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | 56 |
   | `.github/workflows/enhanced-cicd-pipeline.yml` | 9 |
   | `.github/FUTURE_FEATURES_ISSUE.md` | 2 |
   | `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/comprehensive_verification_tests.md` | 2 |
   | `.github/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md` | 1 |
   | `.github/workflows/docs-sync.yml` | 1 -> **0** (this PR) |

   The one in `docs-sync.yml` IS fixed here, because leaving it would have been
   actively harmful: it was inert only while the step 403'd, and repairing the
   permission is exactly what would have started posting it into PR comments.
   `## [BOOK] Documentation Preview` now reads `## [DOCS] Documentation
   Preview`. That is issue #744's rule being defeated by a surface the gate was
   never pointed at, and this PR closes one instance of it, not the class.

## The ruling now lives in a file

Pip's 2026-08-22 ruling existed only in the body of issue #1279, where
`scripts/generate_rulings.py` cannot see it -- it scans the tree, not GitHub.
It is now a one-line `RULING:` declaration in the workflow, next to what it
governs, and shows up under a new `ci-gates` flavour. `RULINGS.md`,
`rulings.json` and the commitment-calendar index are regenerated consequences;
their diffs are line-number shifts only.

Incidental finding worth someone's attention: naming a tool's path inside a
workflow comment made `generate_tools_index.py` record that workflow as a
CALLER of the tool. The comment was reworded to avoid asserting a false edge
into a generated index. A generated index that reads comments cannot tell
"mentions" from "invokes".

## What this PR cannot prove

The workflow only triggers on PRs that touch `godot/scripts/core/game_state.gd`,
`actions.gd`, `events.gd`, `docs/mechanics/**` or the two sync scripts. This PR
touches none of them, so `Documentation Sync` will not run on it and the fix
stays unproven until the next PR that does touch those paths. Verified instead
by: the YAML parsing
(`python -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/docs-sync.yml'))"`),
the resolved per-job permission maps, the token scopes printed in the run
header, and the 403 in real logs. Nobody ran this workflow to green; do not
read the PR as claiming that.

Ladder-Impact: none -- CI workflow permissions and generated doc indexes only; nothing under `godot/` was touched.

issues.title: No tag protection: pushing a release tag needs less review than merging a docs change
issues.body:
## The asymmetry, measured today

`main` is well protected. **Tags are not protected at all.** Releases are built from tags, so the
most privileged act in this repository has less review than merging a documentation change.

Verified against the GitHub API on 2026-08-24 by two seats independently -- found by the pdoom1
seat, re-run by the coordination seat before filing.

| check | command | result |
|---|---|---|
| tag protection rules | `gh api repos/PipFoweraker/pdoom1/tags/protection` | **404 Not Found** -- no rules exist |
| rulesets | `gh api repos/PipFoweraker/pdoom1/rulesets` | one ruleset, id `7544281`, name **"Default no-ruin rules"**, **`enforcement: disabled`**, **`target: branch`** |
| branch protection on `main` | `gh api repos/.../branches/main/protection` | **active and substantial** -- see below |

**What `main` already enforces**, which is the comparison that makes this worth filing:

- 3 required status checks: `GDScript Syntax Check`, `Unit Tests`, `quality-checks`
- required pull request reviews: **1 approving review**, `dismiss_stale_reviews: true`,
  `require_last_push_approval: true`
- `required_linear_history: true`, `allow_force_pushes: false`, `allow_deletions: false`
- `required_conversation_resolution: true`

**So a one-line docs change to `main` needs a passing CI run and an approving review. Pushing a tag
-- which is what causes a public binary to be built and published under Pip's name -- needs
nothing.**

## Two things that make it more than theoretical

**The only ruleset is disabled AND aimed at the wrong target.** "Default no-ruin rules" is
`enforcement: disabled`, so it constrains nothing today; and its `target` is `branch`, so even if it
were enabled it would not cover tags. Enabling it is not the fix on its own.

**`enforce_admins` is `false`** on `main`'s protection. Admin accounts bypass the branch rules that
do exist. Noted for completeness rather than as the headline -- the tag gap stands on its own.

## Why now

A `v0.14.3` tag is expected shortly, to bring players onto the same build the repository is on --
the seed has rolled twice in the repo (`w34` on 23 Aug, `w35` today) and neither roll has reached a
downloadable build. **This issue is not a reason to delay that tag.** It is a reason to know the
gap exists before the release path is exercised, rather than after.

## Suggested remediation, in order of cost

1. **Add a tag protection rule (or a ruleset with `target: tag`) matching `v*`**, restricting who
   may create matching tags. Cheapest change, closes the specific gap.
2. **Decide what "Default no-ruin rules" is for.** A disabled ruleset is worse than no ruleset,
   because it reads as protection in the settings UI while enforcing nothing -- the same defect
   class as a status field that cannot express UNKNOWN. Either enable it or delete it.
3. **Consider `enforce_admins: true`** on `main`, separately and on its own merits.

## Not done here

Nothing was changed. No ruleset was enabled, no protection rule added, no tag pushed. Repository
settings are Pip's alone. This issue records a measurement and a recommendation, nothing more.

issues.title: docs: retire the funder architecture pitch; it asked for a different, larger, older sum
issues.body:
## Decision: RETIRE, not correct

`docs/ARCHITECTURE_FUNDERS.md` was the repository's only funder-facing document, and it
described a **different, larger, older ask** than the one being made this week.

| | This document | The live ask |
|---|---|---|
| Shape | Recurring **annual** funding | **One** all-or-nothing round |
| Amount | $25K / $75K / $150K / **$300K+ per year**, plus a $5K-to-$100K deliverable table | **$14,500 minimum, $48,000 goal** |
| Deadline | none | **2026-09-09** |

The top tier is roughly **20x** the minimum being asked. Pip is driving strangers at this
repo right now; a funder who clicked through to this page read the wrong number.

**Why retire rather than correct.** Reconciling the tiers with the campaign means deleting
the tiers -- there is no version of a four-tier annual ladder that is also a single
all-or-nothing round. What survived that deletion would still be a *second funder-facing
ask* standing beside Manifund, which is the current state and the actual problem. So this
does not split the difference: the rival framework goes, and one ask remains.

## What it claimed, and what is true

Every row checked against the repository on 2026-08-23, not against the document.

| Claim | Reality | Check |
|---|---|---|
| "Windows, Linux, macOS, **Web**" (x3) | **No web export preset exists.** Exactly three: Windows Desktop, Linux/X11, macOS. No workflow performs a Godot export at all. | `grep -E '^(name\|platform)=' godot/export_presets.cfg`; `grep -niE 'web\|html5\|wasm'` on the same file returns nothing; `grep -rniE '\-\-export' .github/workflows/` returns nothing |
| "**Web export**: instant browser play" + "Web export = zero-friction onboarding" | Two of the document's load-bearing *arguments* rest on the build target that does not exist. | as above |
| "$50K / 3 months / **Mobile port**" | No iOS or Android preset either. | `godot/export_presets.cfg` |
| "**v0.11.0**" | `version.txt` = **0.14.3**; newest tag **v0.14.2** | `cat version.txt`; `git tag --sort=-v:refname \| head -1` |
| "**~6,000 lines** GDScript" | **76,949** across 301 files, excl. addons -- **~12.8x** understated | `find godot -name '*.gd' -not -path '*/addons/*' -exec cat {} + \| wc -l` |
| "**30+ tests**" | **1,644** `test_` functions across 166 files | `grep -rhoE '^\s*func test_' <test files> \| wc -l` |
| "**12 workflows**" | **15** | `ls .github/workflows/*.yml \| wc -l` |
| "Builds generated for **all platforms**" (automated) | No workflow runs a Godot export; CI does not build these presets. | `grep -rniE '\-\-export' .github/workflows/` |
| macOS as a shipping platform | **Ad-hoc at best, not notarised**: `codesign/codesign=1`, `codesign/identity=""`, `codesign/apple_team_id=""`, `notarization/notarization=0`. Gatekeeper refuses these without a right-click override. | `grep -nE 'codesign/\|notarization/' godot/export_presets.cfg` |
| "**Open-source**" | Interim **source-available** licence. `docs/copy/budget.json` -> `constraints[1]` forbids the phrase. | budget.json |
| "Production-Ready" x2, "**The architecture is ready**" | `constraints[4]`: no copy may frame p(Doom)1 as a launch, a 1.0, or finished. | budget.json |
| "momentum" doom model | Already flagged retired at `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:11-12`. | that file |
| Footer "Last updated: **2025-12-13**" | Added **2026-07-16** in `5b3159bb`, never modified since. Its self-report and its history disagree. | `git log --diff-filter=A -- docs/ARCHITECTURE_FUNDERS.md` |

**Where the "Web" claim probably came from.** There is a `web_export/` directory in the
repo. It holds one file, `export_summary.json`, dated 2025-10-30 at `v0.10.1`, reading
`"seeds_exported": 0`, `"total_entries": 0`, `"files": []`. It is a **leaderboard-seed
export, not a browser build of the game**, and it is empty. A plausible route to the false
claim is someone reading the directory name. Offered as a hypothesis, not established.

**Not disputed:** the modularity / extension-point description, the data-driven content
argument, and the deterministic-RNG and signal-based-UI points were not re-verified and are
recorded as **UNKNOWN**, not as false.

## What changed

1. **`git mv` to `docs/archive/2026-08-23-architecture-funders/`** -- the retirement route
   `docs/DOC_LIFECYCLE.md` prescribes ("Never delete; `git mv` preserves" `--follow`). The
   body is **unedited**; a header carries the table above so the claims cannot be quietly
   resurrected. `docs/archive/` is excluded from all pre-commit hooks by design.
2. **The old path becomes a signpost, not a second ask.** Two documents already link to it,
   and the retired footer advertised `pdoom.org/donors/architecture`, so deleting the path
   would 404 a funder rather than redirect one. It now carries the campaign link, points at
   **`docs/copy/budget.json` + `tools/render_budget.py` as the single source of truth for
   money**, restates the binding `constraints` block, and states what the build actually is.
   It names **no raised total, no days remaining, and no backer**.
3. **Repointed `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`** -- the banner and open question 3, which had been
   waiting on exactly this call.
4. **Commitment calendar regenerated** -- 156 -> 159 UNPARSED, the three dated lines added here.

## Verification

- `python tools/render_budget.py --check` -> `CHECK OK: 7 line items; min column $14,000,
  goal column $48,000; declared gap $500 reconciles.`
- Full pre-commit suite passes on a complete checkout.

## Notes for Pip

- **Not merged, as instructed.** Opening this PR fires `godot-tests`, `enhanced-cicd-pipeline`,
  `quality-checks` and `self-merge-eligibility` -- all four run on any PR to `main` with no
  path filter, so a docs-only change still triggers a full Godot test run. That is why the
  branch was pushed but the PR was left for you. `self-merge-eligibility` is `contents: read`
  and cannot merge anything.
- **One edit reverted deliberately.** `docs/AGENT_EFFICIENCY_AUDIT.md:147` still advises
  "Leave; maybe add a stale banner" for this document, which undersold it. Updating it is
  blocked by **pre-existing** ASCII debt: the file has 33 non-ASCII lines in `main`, and
  `enforce-standards` fails on `:4` for anyone who touches it. Fixing that is a separable
  cleanup, not this PR's business.
- **`pdoom.org/donors/architecture`** was advertised in the retired footer as a live donor
  route. Whether it still resolves is **UNKNOWN** from here. If it does, it should point at
  the Manifund campaign.
